history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. Can you help?

I can help you troubleshoot your phone’s service and picture messaging issues. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account
- Your customer ID
- Your full name and date of birth

Once I have this information, I’ll guide you through the necessary steps to resolve your service problem.
My name is Sofia Martinez and my phone number is +1-617-555-0148.

Your line is currently suspended, which is why you have no service and cannot send picture messages. However, I see that your recent bills are already paid, so the suspension is not due to an overdue bill.

I can help you further, but first, can you confirm if you recently made any changes to your account or received any notifications about your service? This will help me determine the next steps to restore your service.
I haven't made any changes to my account recently and I haven't received any notifications about my service being suspended.

I have resumed your line, and your service should now be restored. Please reboot your phone to regain service.

After restarting, you should see signal bars and be able to send picture messages again. If you still experience issues after rebooting, let me know and I can assist you further.

history.content: My device rebooted successfully, but I still don't see any signal bars and I can't send picture messages. The issue is not resolved.

Thank you for letting me know. Since your line is now active but you still have no signal or MMS capability, let’s troubleshoot your device settings to identify the cause.

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If Airplane Mode is enabled
- What the signal strength indicator shows (e.g., no signal, 1 bar, etc.)
- If you see any network type (e.g., 5G, 4G, LTE)

If you’re able, please use your device’s diagnostic feature to check the status bar and share the results. This will help me guide you through the next steps.
Actually, I see that Airplane Mode is ON in the status bar, and it also shows No Signal. Should I turn Airplane Mode off?

Yes, please turn Airplane Mode OFF. Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including cellular service, which is why you have no signal.

Once you turn Airplane Mode off, wait a few moments to see if your signal bars return. Let me know if you see any improvement or if you still have issues with service or sending picture messages.
Airplane mode is now OFF, but I still don't see any signal bars and can't send picture messages.

Thank you for updating me. Since Airplane Mode is now off but you still have no signal, the next step is to check your SIM card status. Sometimes, the SIM card may not be properly seated or recognized, which can cause a complete loss of service.

Please check your SIM card status on your device and let me know if it shows as:
- Active
- Missing
- Locked (PIN or PUK required)

If you’re able to use your device’s diagnostic feature to check the SIM status, please do so and share the result. This will help determine the next step to restore your service.
My SIM card status shows as 'Active.' What should I try next?

Since your SIM card is active and Airplane Mode is off, the next step is to check your network settings—specifically, your Access Point Name (APN) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the network and sending picture messages.

Please check your APN settings on your device and let me know if they appear correct or if there are any errors, especially with the MMSC URL (used for picture messaging). If you’re unsure, you can use your device’s diagnostic feature to check the APN settings and share the results. This will help me guide you on whether a reset is needed.
My APN name is fast.telecom.net, but the APN settings status says 'Not set.' The MMSC URL is listed as http://mms.telecom.net/mms/wapenc. What should I do next?

Since your APN settings status says "Not set," this indicates that your APN configuration may be incomplete or incorrect, which can prevent both cellular service and picture messaging from working.

The best next step is to reset your APN settings to the default values. After resetting, you will need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Please reset your APN settings now, then reboot your device. Once your phone restarts, check if you have signal bars and can send picture messages. Let me know the results or if you need guidance on how to reset the APN settings.

I've already reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone. My APN is now set to 'internet' with the MMSC URL as 'http://mms.carrier.com/mms', but there are still no signal bars and I can't send picture messages.
YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
